name: Timeline
purpose: The passive, ordered record of things that have already happened, where the time axis IS the structure: a vertical rail threading date-grouped entries, newest first. Two forms from one grammar — transaction history (status node + amount, the fintech case the itinerary names) and activity feed (actor avatar + what they did).

$differsFromNeighbours.$why: Three gated components already sit close to this one, and a reader will otherwise reach for the wrong one. Stated here because the brief requires a new component to say how it differs from its gated siblings.
$differsFromNeighbours.vs List-items (Transaction row, GATED): List-items is an INTERACTIVE, UNORDERED list — every row is a <button> with hover/pressed/disabled/processing states — and it answers 'which transaction do I want to open?'. Timeline is PASSIVE and ORDERED (<ol>), carries no press states, and answers 'what happened, in what order?'. The tell: remove the ordering from a Timeline and it becomes meaningless; remove it from List-items and nothing is lost. Where a feed genuinely needs each entry to open a detail view, the correct answer is List-items inside a date group — NOT a Timeline that grows buttons. The RAG chip and avatar atoms here are List-items' own, copied verbatim.
$differsFromNeighbours.vs Progress-tracker (GATED, display-only: Visually the closest, and the one most likely to be mistaken for this. Progress-tracker shows a KNOWN, FINITE, FORWARD process with done/current/upcoming steps and a completion the user is travelling toward; it carries aria-current="step" and role="progressbar". Timeline has no current step, no upcoming, no completion and no total — it is open-ended and backward-looking. The rail MECHANISM (li::before connector + node) is Progress-tracker's, rotated to vertical; the SEMANTICS are deliberately not inherited.
$differsFromNeighbours.vs Notifications (GATED, persistent): Notifications are messages awaiting the user's action. A Timeline entry is a record of something already done; it asks nothing.

props.name: form
props.$note: history = status node + amount (transaction history); activity = actor avatar + what they did (activity feed). One grammar, two node treatments.

props.name: status
props.$note: Colours the rail node AND the entry's status chip. The chip always carries a WORD, so the dot never carries meaning alone (s151-D1 clause 4).

props.name: grouped
props.$note: Date group headings ('Today, 19 August'). Ungrouped is legal for short feeds but loses the axis the component exists for.

variants.name: history
variants.use: transaction history — status node, amount, optional explanatory line

variants.name: activity
variants.use: activity feed — actor avatar replaces the status node; who did what, when

variants.name: empty
variants.use: no activity in the window; a single line of prose, no rail

accessibility.structure: An <ol> inside a <section> with a heading, so AT gets both the count and the order for free. Dates are real <time datetime> elements.
accessibility.focus: Entries are NOT focusable — nothing to do on a record. The only focus stop is the optional 'Load older activity' control.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: Every status node dot is accompanied by its RAG tint chip carrying a word — 'Completed', 'Failed', 'Pending', 'Submitted' — per s151-D1 clause 4, where the symbol and label carry meaning and the fill's own contrast is secondary. Neutral label on every RAG tint measures 8.21–14.46 in both modes (measured #203). The warning dot alone is under 3:1, which is precisely why it never travels alone. Dave is astigmatic and red/yellow are problem hues.
accessibility.targetSize: 'Load older activity' is min-height 44px, the ruled min-hit-area, enforced BY HAND — no gate reads the target token.
accessibility.prose: Wrapping description lines use the Editorial composite (.t-ed-body-small) and keep their natural line box (text-box-trim:normal), per the runbook's deciding rule: single-line -> Component, wrapping -> Editorial.

antiPatterns: ⛔ Never put aria-current="step" or role="progressbar" on a Timeline. It borrows Progress-tracker's rail mechanism but has no current step, no total and no completion — those roles would lie to AT.
Never make Timeline entries into buttons. If entries must open, the component you want is List-items inside a date group.
Never let a status dot travel without its word — the warning dot alone is under 3:1 and colour would be the only carrier.
Never reverse the order to oldest-first without changing the date headings with it; the axis is the component.
Never rely on line-height to separate stacked lines — leading-trim is ON, so every stack carries an explicit tokenised gap.
REVIEW Never present the 90-day empty-state window as a product rule; it is invented specimen copy standing in for one.

tokenValidation.result: PASS — snippet gate rc=0, 0 failures on this file. Every declared var matches the store in BOTH modes. No new token minted and none wanted.
tokenValidation.declaredAbsence: The rag-on-neutral pairs (a RAG dot on the card surface) are NOT declared as passing pairs — per s151-D2 that class belongs to the RENDERING gate (_validate_state_contrast.py) where the non-colour carrier is checkable against real DOM. The neutral-label-on-tint pairs ARE declared and pass in both modes.
tokenValidation.reusedVerbatim: Status chip (form B) and avatar disc copied from List-items; rail mechanism copied from Progress-tracker. Both source files untouched.

provenance.$note: Itinerary row 56 (2026-07-14), 'Timeline / activity feed — Transaction history pattern', P2 Depth. Verified absent first-hand #203 (ls + content grep across timeline/activity/feed/history/audit). Built #203 Wave 3b Lane K. No Figma node binds this component.

responsive.container: container-type:inline-size; the entry line collapses title/amount onto separate rows as width falls
responsive.rail: fixed 28px gutter (48px in the avatar form) at every width — the axis must not collapse
responsive.$status: PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed — narrow-viewport reflow below 360px is unexamined and not claimed

dimensions.$note: node 12 and statusDot 8 are graphic marks, not targets. loadMore 44 is the ruled min-hit-area.

$openQuestions: The 12px rail node and the 8px status dot are ROUND. That is a reading of the angular rule, not a ruled exemption — Avatar and Badge are the two documented ones. Square nodes are equally buildable; Dave's eye is owed.
Newest-first ordering is asserted here, not ruled.
Whether the activity form should also carry a status node alongside the avatar (both, or avatar only) is unresolved; the specimen shows avatar only.
